**Finding: compliant (no redline proposed).**

The agreement contains no audit, inspection, verification or records-access right running against Mortgage Logic.com. I checked the compensation section (§5–6), the Client covenants (§8), the licence and hosting sections (§2–4), confidentiality (§10), and the general/boilerplate provisions (§12–30), plus the definitions — none creates a TrueLink audit, on-site inspection, or usage-verification right.

Points worth noting:
- Fees are invoiced by TrueLink under §5(a), so there is no Client self-reporting regime that would attract a verification right.
- The information-flow provisions run in our favour: §6 requires TrueLink to give us documentation supporting its charges plus a contest right, and §3(e) gives us real-time access to usage statistics and raw log files.
- §8(f) (anti-spam technical mechanisms) operates on TrueLink's own hosted environment; it is not an audit of our records and gives no access to our systems, so it is not responsive to this rule and is covered by the separate anti-spam covenant.

Because the absence of any audit right leaves us better off than the preferred position, no change is warranted — adding audit machinery would create a Vendor right we do not currently face. Flagged only as a watch item: if the pricing exhibits are completed with self-reported per-transaction volumes, we should resist any new audit right or hold it to once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, off-site, independent auditor bound by confidentiality, at TrueLink's cost absent 5% underpayment.
